security_audit.summary: All 31 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, TypeScript template literals, ordinary variable names, and documentation keywords. No prompt injection or credential exfiltration intent was found. One medium semantic risk remains because the self-modification example can encourage destructive repository rollback without explicit user approval.

remediation.issue: Self-modification guidance includes a hard-reset rollback example.
remediation.suggestion: Replace hard reset with a user-approved rollback plan, preserve uncommitted work, and require explicit confirmation before destructive git operations.

remediation.issue: Documentation discusses YOLO orchestration and self-modifying agents.
remediation.suggestion: State that production systems should default to safety-first or hybrid approval for shell, write, and repository operations.

content.value_statement: Multi-agent projects often fail from unclear orchestration, weak boundaries, and unmanaged tool access. This skill provides architecture patterns, safety controls, and production checklists for coordinated agents.
actual_capabilities: Guides discovery questions for scale, state, tool access, and coordination constraints.
Explains a four-layer architecture with deterministic tools below the reasoning layer.
Compares seven coordination patterns, including fan-out, pipelines, delegation, queues, map-reduce, peer review, and MAKER.
Provides implementation guidance for permission inheritance, locks, rate limits, caching, and sub-agents as tools.
Covers production controls such as cascading stop, orphan detection, checkpointing, cost tracking, and self-modification review.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a complete runnable framework.
The code examples need adaptation to the target language, runtime, and security model.
High-stakes medical, legal, or financial use needs domain review and external validation.
Cost and reliability estimates are illustrative and should be tested with real workloads.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Agent Platform
use_cases.description: Define orchestration layers, agent roles, tool boundaries, and lifecycle rules before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Harden Existing Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Add cleanup, checkpointing, rate limits, cost tracking, and permission controls to an active multi-agent system.

use_cases.title: Choose Coordination Patterns
use_cases.description: Compare parallel, sequential, recursive, queue-based, and voting approaches for a specific product workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Start With Discovery
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a multi-agent system. Ask the required discovery questions first, then recommend an initial architecture.

prompt_templates.title: Select a Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare fan-out, sequential pipeline, recursive delegation, work queue, map-reduce, peer collaboration, and MAKER for my workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Design Tool Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Design the tool coordination model for this agent system, including permissions, locks, rate limits, caching, and cleanup rules.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this multi-agent design for production readiness. Check cascading stop, orphan detection, checkpoints, cost tracking, and self-modification controls.

output_examples.input: I need agents to review many pull request files in parallel.
output_examples.output: Recommended a batched fan-out and fan-in design with specialist reviewers, timeouts, cost tracking, and cascading cleanup.

output_examples.input: My agent workflow loses progress when a session crashes.
output_examples.output: Outlined checkpoint triggers, a project-level task store, stale task release, and recovery steps for claimed work.

output_examples.input: Several agents need access to the same rate-limited API.
output_examples.output: Suggested shared token buckets, permission inheritance, cache rules, and lock ownership checks for coordinated access.

best_practices: Ask the discovery questions before selecting a coordination pattern.
Keep tools deterministic and place LLM calls in orchestration or reasoning layers.
Add lifecycle cleanup, permission limits, timeouts, and cost tracking before production use.
anti_patterns: Spawning unbounded agents without batching, depth limits, or cost controls.
Letting child agents inherit write or shell permissions they do not need.
Using self-modifying agents without tests, branch isolation, approval gates, and rollback planning.

faq.question: Does this skill provide runnable code?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture guidance and illustrative TypeScript examples that need project-specific implementation.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: When should I use MAKER?
faq.answer: Use it only when tasks decompose cleanly, validation is deterministic, and correctness matters more than speed or cost.

faq.question: Does it cover production operations?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers cascading stop, orphan detection, checkpointing, cost tracking, task stores, and coordination primitives.

faq.question: Can it help with tool permissions?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains permission inheritance, read-only sub-agents, lock ownership, rate limiting, and cache invalidation.

faq.question: Is it safe for high-stakes domains?
faq.answer: It can help structure designs, but high-stakes deployments need domain experts, validation, monitoring, and approval controls.
